intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer 2026, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, towering limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boat tours depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets. Sample local cheeses, olives, cured meats, fresh seafood, and traditional Greek street food like souvlaki and spanakopita. Engage with local vendors and discover authentic Greek culinary culture in one of Athens' oldest markets.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow crystal-clear lagoon. Wade through the warm, knee-deep waters to reach the small island of Elafonissi. The unique pink sand comes from crushed shells and coral, making this one of Europe's most unique beach experiences.

experiences.name: Traditional Cretan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in Crete to learn how to prepare authentic Cretan dishes such as dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi (wild greens), and loukoumades (honey doughnuts). Visit a local market beforehand to select fresh ingredients, and enjoy your meal with local wine or raki at the end of the session.

experiences.name: Sunset Dinner at a Santorini Taverna
experiences.description: Experience a traditional Greek dinner at a cliffside taverna in Oia while watching one of the world's most famous sunsets. Feast on fresh grilled octopus, fava (yellow split pea dip), fresh fish, and local Assyrtiko white wine. The combination of spectacular caldera views, golden light, and authentic Cycladic cuisine makes this an unforgettable evening.

weather.summary: Hot and sunny. Sea warm enough for swimming.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect baggage, and take the X96 express bus or Metro Line 3 to your connection point toward Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In flight
meals.lunch: N/A - In flight
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night snack from a 24-hour kiosk (periptero) near the hotel or airport — try a tiropita (cheese pie) or spanakopita for under €2. Stay hydrated after the flight.

day_by_day.notes: Keep your first night simple. Have local currency (euros) ready before leaving the airport. The X96 bus from Athens airport costs around €6 and runs 24 hours. Confirm hotel late check-in arrangements in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, take a relaxed walk along the beachfront to get your bearings. Explore the immediate area around Aegean Bliss Resort, locate nearby shops, bakeries, and the beach access points.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest public beach. With sea temperatures warm and skies sunny (avg high 29°C), this is perfect for your first swim in Greece. Bring a reusable water bottle and sunscreen. Relax on the sand and soak in the atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the local village or waterfront promenade. Look for a family-run taverna for your first proper Greek dinner. Order simply — grilled fish, Greek salad, and house wine or local beer.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or visit a local bakery for fresh koulouri (sesame bread ring) and Greek coffee — budget around €3–4.
meals.lunch: Pick up fresh fruit, olives, and local cheese from a nearby mini-market for a beach picnic — budget €5–6.
meals.dinner: Family taverna dinner: Greek salad (€5), grilled chicken or souvlaki (€7), and local draft beer (€3) — total around €15–16.

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is your orientation and recovery day. Don't over-schedule. Pick up a local SIM card if you haven't already — Cosmote or Vodafone Greece offer tourist SIMs for around €10–15 with data.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early and visit the local morning market (laiki agora) if one is operating nearby. These weekly street markets sell fresh produce, olives, honey, herbs, and local cheeses at very low prices. Great for stocking up on budget snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Beach day at a nearby cove or less-crowded stretch of coastline. Ask hotel staff for their recommendation on a quieter beach within walking or short bus distance. Bring snorkeling gear if you have it — Greek waters are crystal clear.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local neighborhood on foot. Find a small souvlaki stand or gyros shop for a casual, authentic, and very affordable dinner.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts from a local café — budget €3–5.
meals.lunch: Fresh bread, tomatoes, feta, and olives purchased from the morning market — budget €4–5.
meals.dinner: Pork gyros wrap with tzatziki and fries from a local souvlaki shop — budget €3–4 per wrap. One of Greece's best budget meals.

day_by_day.notes: Markets typically run Tuesday, Friday, or Saturday mornings depending on the area. Confirm the local market schedule with hotel staff. Bring a reusable bag for market shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or affordable taxi to explore a nearby town or village. Visit the main square (plateia), a local church or small archaeological site, and browse any craft or local produce shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Find a beach near the village you're visiting. Many Greek coastal towns have easily accessible public beaches with free entry. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing before heading back.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Enjoy a sunset walk along the waterfront. Try ouzo or tsipouro at a local kafeneion (traditional Greek café) — a very cheap and authentic experience.

meals.breakfast: Grab a bougatsa (custard-filled pastry) and Greek coffee from a local bakery — budget €3–4.
meals.lunch: Eat at a cheap local taverna in the village — ask for the daily special (mageirefta), which are pre-cooked traditional dishes and very affordable. Budget €7–9 for a full meal.
meals.dinner: Light mezedes (small plates) at a kafeneion: olives, taramosalata, bread — budget €8–10 with a drink.

day_by_day.notes: Mageirefta (oven-cooked dishes) like moussaka, fasolada, and stifado are the cheapest and most authentic options at Greek tavernas. Always ask what the daily special is.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning swim before the beach gets crowded — the sea is warm and calm in the morning. After swimming, take a coastal walk and enjoy the scenery. Bring water and sunscreen.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local fishing harbor if one is nearby. Watch the fishermen and browse any fresh catch being sold directly from boats. This is a great cultural experience and photo opportunity.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a simple meal if your accommodation has kitchen access (buy ingredients at a local mini-market), or find a budget-friendly psarotaverna (fish taverna) near the harbor for fresh grilled fish.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered: Greek yogurt, honey, fruit, and instant coffee from mini-market supplies — budget €2–3.
meals.lunch: Freshly caught grilled octopus or sardines from a harbor-side snack stall — budget €5–8.
meals.dinner: Psarotaverna: grilled sea bream (tsipoura) with lemon and olive oil, village salad, and local white wine — budget €14–18.

day_by_day.notes: Sardines (sardeles) and mackerel (skoumbri) are the most affordable fresh fish options at Greek fish restaurants. Avoid tourist-trap restaurants near major landmarks — walk one or two streets back for better prices.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip planning day. Use the morning to research and arrange a budget day trip — either a local boat trip to a nearby island or beach (often €15–25 return), or a bus trip to a nearby archaeological site or scenic town.
day_by_day.afternoon: If a boat trip is arranged, spend the afternoon exploring a nearby islet or secluded beach only accessible by sea. Swim in turquoise waters and enjoy the scenery. Alternatively, visit a local olive grove or vineyard for a free or low-cost self-guided walk.
day_by_day.evening: Return by early evening. Treat yourself to a proper sit-down dinner at a mid-range taverna — you've been eating well on budget all week, so a slightly nicer dinner is still affordable.

meals.breakfast: Koulouri and coffee from a street vendor — budget €2.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic for the boat trip: bread, cheese, fruit, and water from the mini-market — budget €5.
meals.dinner: Taverna dinner: moussaka or pastitsio, Greek salad, local wine — budget €15–18.

day_by_day.notes: Check local travel agencies or the hotel reception for affordable day-trip boat excursions. Group boat trips are much cheaper than private charters. Book the evening before to secure a spot.

day_by_day.morning: Mid-trip rest and recharge day. Sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, and spend the morning reading or relaxing on the hotel beach or by the pool. Greece rewards those who slow down.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to a nearby beach you haven't visited yet. Try paddleboarding or kayaking if rentals are available — usually €10–15/hour. Alternatively, explore rock pools and snorkel in shallow coves.
day_by_day.evening: Join locals for the evening volta (traditional evening stroll) along the promenade. Stop for ice cream (pagoto) from a local gelateria — Greek ice cream is excellent and costs €1.50–2.50 per scoop.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a full Greek breakfast at a café: eggs, local sausage, tomatoes, feta, bread — budget €6–8.
meals.lunch: Cheese or spinach pie (tiropita/spanakopita) from a local bakery, plus a cold frappe coffee — budget €4–5.
meals.dinner: Casual souvlaki dinner with a cold Mythos or Alfa beer — budget €8–10.

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 marks the halfway point. Take stock of your budget spending so far. Greek bakeries (fournos) are your best friend for cheap, filling, and delicious food throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a nearby historic church, Byzantine chapel, or small local museum. Many smaller Greek museums charge €2–5 entry or are free. These offer great insight into local history and culture without breaking the budget.
day_by_day.afternoon: Beach afternoon at your favorite spot discovered during the week. The water is warm (sea temperatures peak in June) — perfect for long swims. Try to find a beach bar that doesn't charge for sunbeds, or bring your own towel.
day_by_day.evening: Find a rooftop or hillside spot to watch the sunset — one of Greece's most spectacular free experiences. Bring a local wine or beer from the mini-market (€2–3) and enjoy.

meals.breakfast: Greek coffee and a sweet bougatsa from a local café — budget €3–4.
meals.lunch: Village salad (horiatiki) and grilled pita with tzatziki at a local taverna — budget €8–10.
meals.dinner: Lentil soup (fakes) and bread at a traditional taverna — one of Greece's most beloved and cheapest dishes, budget €6–8.

day_by_day.notes: Lentil soup (fakes) is a staple of Greek home cooking and extremely cheap at traditional tavernas. Don't overlook vegetarian Greek dishes — they are delicious and very affordable.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus to explore a different coastal area or inland village within the region. Walk through narrow whitewashed alleys, visit the local church square, and talk to locals at the kafeneion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Find a beach near your exploration area. Many less-touristed beaches in Greece are free, uncrowded, and stunningly beautiful. Spend a few hours swimming and relaxing before the return trip.
day_by_day.evening: Back at the resort area, visit a local taverna known for grilled meats. Order a mixed grill platter to share if dining with a companion, or a single lamb chop (paidakia) with roasted potatoes.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered breakfast from mini-market supplies — yogurt, honey, bread — budget €2–3.
meals.lunch: Cheap local eatery in the village: stuffed tomatoes or peppers (gemista), bread, and water — budget €7–9.
meals.dinner: Grilled lamb chops with lemon potatoes and a village salad — budget €14–17.

day_by_day.notes: Local KTEL buses in Greece are very affordable (usually €2–6 for regional routes) and a great way to explore beyond the immediate resort area. Check timetables the day before as schedules can be infrequent.

day_by_day.morning: Morning snorkeling session at a rocky cove or clear-water beach. Greek waters in June are exceptionally clear. Look for sea urchins, small fish, and octopus among the rocks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local olive oil producer, honey farm, or winery if one is accessible nearby. Many offer free or very low-cost tastings and are fascinating cultural experiences. Ask hotel staff for local recommendations.
day_by_day.evening: Pick up local food souvenirs from a deli or mini-market: small jars of thyme honey, local oregano, olive oil, or ouzo. These make great gifts and are far cheaper than tourist shops.

meals.breakfast: Sesame koulouri and a Greek iced coffee (frappe) from a street kiosk — budget €2–3.
meals.lunch: Dakos (Cretan rusk salad with tomatoes and feta) at a local café — budget €5–7.
meals.dinner: Taverna dinner: slow-cooked lamb with orzo (arni me kritharaki) and local red wine — budget €14–16.

day_by_day.notes: Thyme honey from Greece is world-renowned and very affordable when bought locally (€4–8 for a small jar). Avoid airport shops for food souvenirs — prices are significantly higher.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach morning — revisit your favorite beach of the trip. Swim, sunbathe, and take photos. Reflect on the best moments of the journey so far.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local market or shopping street for any last-minute gifts or personal items. Visit a local ceramics or craft shop to browse handmade goods. Even window shopping is enjoyable in Greek towns.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer dinner at a well-reviewed local taverna. Order dishes you haven't tried yet — perhaps fresh grilled octopus, saganaki (fried cheese), or shrimp saganaki.

meals.breakfast: Full Greek café breakfast: eggs, feta, tomatoes, olives, bread, coffee — budget €6–8.
meals.lunch: Gyros wrap or souvlaki from your favorite local spot — budget €3–5.
meals.dinner: Celebratory taverna meal: saganaki, grilled octopus, main dish, dessert (galaktoboureko), and local wine — budget €22–28 as a treat.

day_by_day.notes: Galaktoboureko (custard pastry in syrup) is a must-try Greek dessert. Many tavernas offer it complimentary at the end of a meal as a gesture of hospitality (filoxenia). Don't refuse!

day_by_day.morning: Last full morning in Greece. Take a final sunrise or early morning walk along the beach. Swim one last time in the warm Aegean. Take in the views and atmosphere mindfully.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin packing and organizing belongings. Do a final check of your budget — calculate what you've spent and what remains. Use remaining euros on local snacks, coffee, or small gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Greece — return to your favorite taverna from the trip or try somewhere new. Enjoy a leisurely meal, order a carafe of local wine, and toast to a wonderful trip.

meals.breakfast: Last Greek bakery breakfast: bougatsa and strong Greek coffee — budget €3–4.
meals.lunch: Light mezedes spread: tzatziki, taramosalata, olives, grilled pita — budget €10–12.
meals.dinner: Farewell taverna dinner: your favorite dish from the trip plus a Greek dessert and coffee — budget €18–22.

day_by_day.notes: Greek coffee (ellinikos kafes) served with a glass of cold water is a beautiful tradition. Always sip the water first, then enjoy the coffee slowly. A perfect final evening ritual.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy one last coffee and pastry from a local café near the hotel. Take a final stroll to the beach for a last look at the Aegean Sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to the airport or departure point. Allow plenty of time for transfers. Use public transport (bus or metro) to keep costs low on the way out, just as on arrival.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Greece. Reflect on 13 days of beaches, local food, warm hospitality, and Mediterranean sunshine. Carry home your food souvenirs, memories, and a deep appreciation for Greek culture.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek coffee and koulouri from a street kiosk near the hotel — budget €2–3.
meals.lunch: Light snack at the airport or pack leftovers from mini-market supplies — budget €5–8.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination.

day_by_day.notes: Keep €20–30 in euros for airport expenses and last-minute transport. Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure. Take one last deep breath of sea air before you go — you'll want to remember it.

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront room. Take a brief stroll on the hotel terrace to enjoy the night sea breeze.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night snack at the hotel bar or a light mezze platter from room service upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — focus on arrival and rest. Confirm your transfer or taxi booking in advance. The hotel check-in desk is typically open 24 hours at resort properties.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hotel. After breakfast, take your first walk along the resort's beachfront. Dip your toes in the warm Aegean Sea and get oriented with the surrounding area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest local beach (ask hotel concierge for the best spot within walking or short taxi distance). Swim, sunbathe, and relax. Rent a sun lounger and umbrella for around €8–12. Explore the beach promenade and browse local shops.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the nearest village or town center for your first authentic Greek dinner. Look for a family-run taverna with outdoor seating.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy Greek yogurt with honey, fresh fruit, and pastries
meals.lunch: Beachside snack bar — try a gyros wrap or a fresh Greek salad (€6–10)
meals.dinner: Local taverna — order grilled octopus, tzatziki, fresh bread, and a glass of local white wine (€20–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Apply high-SPF sunscreen from the start — the June sun is intense. Stay hydrated throughout the day. This is your orientation day, so keep it relaxed.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning swim before the beach gets crowded — the sea is warm and calm at this hour. Return for breakfast, then join a local guided walking tour of the nearest historic town or village to get cultural context for your surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local archaeological site, ancient ruins, or a hilltop viewpoint accessible from your area. Explore at your own pace and take in panoramic views of the Aegean. Stop at a local kafeneion (coffee house) for a Greek frappé.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the beachfront area for a sunset cocktail at a clifftop or waterfront bar. Watch the famous Greek sunset over the sea.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — try spanakopita (spinach pie) if available, or head to a local bakery for fresh tiropita and coffee
meals.lunch: Traditional Greek souvlaki place in the village — souvlaki plate with pita, tomatoes, and onions (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Seaside restaurant — fresh grilled fish of the day, horiatiki salad, and local retsina wine (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the historic town tour. Bring a light layer for the evening as sea breezes can be refreshing after sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip by local ferry or boat to a nearby smaller island or secluded cove. Depart early to maximize time. Enjoy the scenic boat ride across the Aegean with stunning blue water views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the smaller island or cove — swim in crystal-clear turquoise water, snorkel if gear is available to rent, and wander through any charming whitewashed streets or fishing harbors.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry in the late afternoon or early evening. Freshen up at the hotel and enjoy a quiet dinner close to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before departure — grab a pastry and coffee to go
meals.lunch: Lunch at a harborside taverna on the island — try fresh calamari, grilled sardines, and a village salad (€15–22 per person)
meals.dinner: Relaxed dinner at a restaurant near the hotel — try moussaka or pastitsio, a classic Greek comfort dish (€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check the ferry schedule the evening before and book tickets in advance if possible. Bring sunscreen, a hat, water, and a small backpack. Snorkeling gear can often be rented on the island for €5–10.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local morning market (laiki agora) — browse stalls selling fresh produce, olives, local cheeses, honey, and herbs. This is a great opportunity to interact with locals and pick up picnic supplies or edible souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a quieter, less-touristy beach recommended by locals. Spend the afternoon swimming, reading, and relaxing in the sun. If available in the area, try a paddleboard or kayak rental for €15–20/hour.
day_by_day.evening: Join a local cooking class or food experience if available nearby (book in advance). Learn to make traditional dishes like spanakopita, tzatziki, or a classic Greek salad. Alternatively, explore the local restaurant scene independently.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at the market — fresh bread, local olives, feta cheese, and a coffee from a nearby café (€5–8)
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach with market finds — olives, cheese, bread, tomatoes, and fruit
meals.dinner: Cooking class dinner (if booked) or a meze dinner at a local restaurant — order a spread of small dishes to share: dolmades, hummus, grilled halloumi, and loukoumades for dessert (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Morning markets typically run from 7:00–14:00. Arrive early for the best selection. Cooking classes in Greece often cost €50–80 per person and are well worth the experience.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter, ATV, or car for the day to explore the wider region at your own pace. Drive along coastal roads, stopping at viewpoints, hidden beaches, and small fishing villages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Discover a hidden or less-visited beach along the coastal route. Swim and relax. Stop at a small fishing village for a coffee break and a chat with locals if possible.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel and enjoy a swim in the resort pool or sea as the sun lowers. Get ready for a slightly more special dinner to mark the midpoint of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fuel up before your driving day
meals.lunch: Small village taverna along your route — try whatever the daily special is, often a slow-cooked stew or grilled lamb chops (€12–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly upscale beachfront restaurant — fresh lobster pasta or grilled sea bass, with a bottle of local Assyrtiko white wine (€35–45 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Scooter rental typically costs €20–35/day; car rental €40–60/day. Bring your driving license. GPS or offline maps are essential. Fill up on fuel before heading into rural areas.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge day. Enjoy a slow morning at the hotel — lounge by the pool, read, or take a gentle yoga stretch on the beach. This is your halfway point, so take it easy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local museum, Byzantine church, or cultural site in the nearest town. Spend an hour or two absorbing Greek history and art. Browse local artisan shops for handmade ceramics, jewelry, or woven goods.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise if available in the area (book through the hotel concierge). Enjoy a 2-hour boat trip along the coastline with wine and snacks as the sun sets over the Aegean.

meals.breakfast: Extended hotel breakfast — take your time and enjoy every option on the buffet
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café in town — a Greek sandwich (dakos) with barley rusk, tomatoes, and feta, plus a cold lemonade (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Post-cruise dinner at a harbor restaurant — grilled prawns, Greek salad, and baklava for dessert (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sunset cruises typically cost €30–60 per person and last 2–3 hours. Book at least a day in advance. The summer solstice is on or around June 21 — one of the longest days of the year, perfect for a sunset cruise.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning hike or coastal walk along a scenic trail near the hotel. The cooler morning air (before 10:00) is ideal for walking. Enjoy wildflowers, sea views, and the sounds of nature waking up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to a favorite beach from earlier in the trip or try a new one. Spend the afternoon fully relaxing — this is your beach bliss afternoon. Try snorkeling if you haven't yet.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local nightlife scene — visit a rooftop bar or a lively taverna with live Greek music. Many Greek restaurants host live bouzouki music in the evenings during summer.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the hike — yogurt, fruit, and coffee at the hotel
meals.lunch: Beach taverna — fresh fish soup (kakavia), grilled vegetables, and crusty bread (€14–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Lively taverna with live music — enjoy a full meze spread: taramosalata, grilled meats, pita, and a carafe of local house wine (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear proper shoes for the coastal hike and bring water. Live music tavernas often get going after 21:00 — Greeks dine late, so don't rush your evening.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to a nearby town or city of cultural significance — this could be an ancient city, a Byzantine settlement, or a vibrant port town depending on your location. Travel by local bus or taxi.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the day-trip destination. Visit its main archaeological site, wander its old town streets, and browse local shops. Try a local specialty snack unique to that area.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel by early evening. Enjoy a quiet dinner close to the resort and an early night to rest your feet.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Restaurant in the day-trip town — try a regional specialty dish you haven't had yet, such as lamb kleftiko or stuffed tomatoes (gemista) (€15–22 per person)
meals.dinner: Simple and satisfying dinner near the hotel — grilled chicken souvlaki plate, tzatziki, and a beer (€15–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Research the day-trip destination in advance and note opening hours for archaeological sites (most open 08:00–20:00 in summer). Carry a reusable water bottle and wear a hat.

day_by_day.morning: Water sports morning — try jet skiing, parasailing, or a banana boat ride at the beach. Most beach resorts in Greece have water sports operators set up from around 09:00. Budget €20–50 depending on activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax and recover from the morning's excitement with a long, lazy beach afternoon. Read, nap, swim, and soak up the sun. Order a cold Mythos beer or fresh lemonade from the beach bar.
day_by_day.evening: Explore a different part of the local town or resort area you haven't visited yet. Find a new restaurant for dinner and try something from the menu you've been curious about.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — load up on protein before water sports
meals.lunch: Beach bar lunch — a club sandwich or a Greek wrap with fries and a cold drink (€10–14)
meals.dinner: New restaurant discovery — try fresh pasta with seafood (a Greek-Italian coastal influence) or a traditional lamb dish with roasted potatoes (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Water sports operators are usually located directly on the main beach. Prices are often negotiable if you want to try multiple activities. Always follow safety instructions.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to souvenir shopping and exploring local artisan boutiques. Look for authentic Greek products: extra virgin olive oil, thyme honey, saffron, handmade sandals, ceramic pottery, and evil eye charms.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local winery or olive oil producer if one is accessible from your area (the hotel concierge can recommend options). Take a short tour and enjoy a tasting session — a wonderful way to connect with Greek agricultural traditions.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style dinner with a special atmosphere — choose a restaurant with a stunning sea view or romantic terrace setting to celebrate a wonderful trip.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast in town — freddo espresso or cappuccino, a bougatsa (cream-filled pastry) or koulouri (sesame bread ring) (€5–8)
meals.lunch: Light mezze lunch at the winery or a nearby café — local cheeses, cured meats, olives, and wine (€15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Special dinner at a top-rated local restaurant — whole grilled fish, risotto with seafood, fine Greek wine, and a dessert of galaktoboureko (custard pastry) (€35–50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Many local producers offer free or low-cost tastings. Call ahead or ask the hotel to arrange a visit. For souvenir shopping, avoid tourist traps near major landmarks — the best quality goods are found in smaller artisan shops.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach morning — return to your favorite beach spot one last time. Swim, float, and soak in the Aegean warmth. Take photos, journal, and be fully present in this beautiful setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore any remaining spots on your list — a café you wanted to try, a viewpoint you passed by, or a shop you meant to revisit. Pack any purchased items carefully in the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Casual, relaxed final dinner in Greece. Choose a comfortable, familiar spot — perhaps the first taverna you loved on Day 2 — and enjoy a nostalgic last meal.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — enjoy every last bite of Greek yogurt and honey
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a beach café — shrimp saganaki (prawns in tomato and feta sauce) with crusty bread and a cold drink (€15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Final Greek dinner at a beloved local taverna — order your favorites from the trip: grilled octopus, horiatiki salad, fresh fish, and a dessert of loukoumades (honey doughnuts) (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Begin packing this evening. Confirm your departure transfer or taxi for the following day. Check the hotel's checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for one last sunrise walk along the beach or hotel terrace. Breathe in the sea air and take a final swim if time allows before checkout. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Transfer to the airport based on your flight time. Allow extra time for traffic and airport procedures. Browse duty-free for any last-minute Greek treats — olive oil, wine, or honey make great gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Greece with incredible memories of beaches, food, sunsets, and warm Aegean hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savor every last bite
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or café — grab a final Greek coffee and a snack before boarding
meals.dinner: On the plane or at your destination

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure. Keep all receipts for any tax-free shopping claims. Double-check that you haven't left anything at the hotel — especially items left on the beach or by the pool.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, towering limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boat tours depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets. Sample local cheeses, olives, cured meats, fresh seafood, and traditional Greek street food like souvlaki and spanakopita. Engage with local vendors and discover authentic Greek culinary culture in one of Athens' oldest markets.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow crystal-clear lagoon. Wade through the warm, knee-deep waters to reach the small island of Elafonissi. The unique pink sand comes from crushed shells and coral, making this one of Europe's most unique beach experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled – late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. A private luxury transfer will be waiting to escort you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, enjoy a welcome drink at the resort's bar, and settle into your beachfront suite.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light late-night welcome snack platter and complimentary champagne provided by the resort upon check-in

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private airport transfer with the resort. Confirm early check-in or luggage storage if needed. Keep Day 1 light – rest is the priority after a long flight.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort's beachfront restaurant. Afterward, take a relaxing stroll along the private beach, soak in your first Greek sunrise over the Aegean, and take a refreshing morning dip in the warm sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon by the resort's infinity pool or on the private beach. Arrange a premium sunbed and cabana service. Optionally book a 90-minute couples' or solo massage at the resort spa to recover from jet lag.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a nearby upscale taverna for your first authentic Greek dinner. Explore the local harbor area if the resort is coastal, enjoying the golden-hour views before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Lavish buffet breakfast at the resort's beachfront restaurant featuring fresh pastries, Greek yogurt with Cretan honey, seasonal fruits, smoked salmon, and made-to-order eggs
meals.lunch: Light mezze lunch at the resort's pool bar – grilled octopus, tzatziki, spanakopita, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at a premium local seafood restaurant near the resort – fresh catch of the day, grilled sea bass, lobster pasta, and a curated Greek wine list

day_by_day.notes: This is an orientation and recovery day. No heavy sightseeing planned. Confirm upcoming excursion bookings with the resort concierge today.

day_by_day.morning: Athens Central Market Food Tour: Start the morning with a private guided food tour of the Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market). Explore the vibrant stalls of fresh fish, meats, spices, olives, and cheeses. Sample local delicacies including loukoumades, freshly cut charcuterie, and artisanal Greek cheeses. A private car or luxury transfer from the resort is recommended.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the food tour, explore the Monastiraki and Plaka neighborhoods. Browse artisan shops and boutiques for premium Greek olive oil, saffron, and local ceramics. Visit the iconic Acropolis and Parthenon with a private guide for a premium, crowd-free experience (book early morning or afternoon slot).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area for a sunset cocktail on the terrace. Dine at a rooftop restaurant in Athens or near the resort with panoramic views.

meals.breakfast: Greek breakfast at the resort before departure – feta omelette, village bread, fresh orange juice, and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Mezze lunch included as part of the Athens Central Market Food Tour – sample spreads, cured meats, olives, and local wines at a traditional ouzeri
meals.dinner: Rooftop fine dining restaurant in Athens – contemporary Greek cuisine featuring lamb chops with herb crust, grilled prawns, and an extensive Greek wine selection. Recommended: Varoulko Seaside or Hytra Restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Book the Athens Central Market Food Tour and Acropolis private guide in advance. Arrange a private luxury vehicle for the day trip to Athens. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the market and Acropolis tour.

day_by_day.morning: Private yacht charter morning: Depart from the nearest marina for a private half-day yacht excursion along the Saronic Gulf or local coastline. Swim in secluded crystal-clear coves, snorkel over rocky reefs, and enjoy the Aegean breeze with a chilled bottle of Assyrtiko wine on deck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort by early afternoon. Relax on the private beach, enjoy water sports offered by the resort (paddleboarding, kayaking, or jet skiing). Take advantage of the warm 29°C weather for extended beach time.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private Greek cooking class at a premium local culinary studio or at the resort. Learn to prepare classic dishes such as moussaka, fresh tzatziki, and baklava under the guidance of a professional Greek chef.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort – Greek yogurt parfait, honey and walnut cake, fresh fruit platter, and espresso
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch prepared by the resort served aboard the private yacht – cold cuts, artisan bread, grilled vegetables, marinated seafood, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Enjoy the dishes prepared during your cooking class as your dinner, paired with premium Greek wines selected by the culinary instructor

day_by_day.notes: Book the private yacht charter at least 48 hours in advance through the resort concierge. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and reef-safe swimming gear. The cooking class typically lasts 2–3 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby ancient archaeological site or historic village. If based near Athens, visit Cape Sounion and the Temple of Poseidon via private car for a breathtaking clifftop experience overlooking the Aegean Sea. Alternatively, visit Delphi for a premium guided archaeological tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the surrounding area. Stop at a traditional Greek village for a leisurely walk through cobblestone streets, visit a local monastery, and browse a weekly farmers' market if available. Sample local thyme honey and handmade preserves.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a sunset swim. Dine at the resort's signature fine dining restaurant for an elevated Greek gastronomy experience.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast – eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, freshly baked croissants, cold-pressed juices, and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Traditional taverna lunch in the village near Cape Sounion or Delphi – grilled sardines, horiatiki salad, fresh pita, and local house wine
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant – tasting menu featuring seven courses of modern Greek cuisine, paired with curated wines from Santorini, Nemea, and Crete

day_by_day.notes: Cape Sounion is approximately 70 km from Athens – allow 1.5 hours each way by private car. Sunset at Cape Sounion is spectacular; time your visit accordingly. Book dinner reservation at the resort restaurant in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Fly or take a high-speed ferry to Zakynthos (Zante) for a two-night island experience. Arrange a private transfer to your premium accommodation or a luxury boutique hotel on the island. Check in and freshen up before heading out.
day_by_day.afternoon: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit: Board a private or small-group boat tour from the port of Zakynthos to the iconic Navagio Beach. Marvel at the dramatic limestone cliffs, the famous shipwreck embedded in the white sand, and the impossibly turquoise waters. Swim and snorkel in the stunning cove.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Zakynthos Town (Zante Town). Stroll along the Venetian-influenced harbor, explore the Bochali Hill for panoramic views, and enjoy a relaxed dinner at a harbor-front restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departure – yogurt, honey, fresh fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch on the boat during the Navagio Beach excursion – fresh sandwiches, local cheese, olives, fruits, and chilled water provided by the tour operator
meals.dinner: Dinner at a premium seafood restaurant in Zakynthos Town – grilled lobster, stuffed squid, and local Zakynthian wines. Recommended: Varkarola Restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Book the Navagio boat tour in advance as spots are limited. Wear water shoes as the beach has coarse sand and pebbles. Bring waterproof sunscreen and a dry bag for valuables. The boat tour typically lasts 3–4 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Blue Caves of Zakynthos on a morning boat excursion along the northern coastline. The sea caves glow with brilliant blue light due to sunlight refracting through the water – most vivid in the morning hours. Swim inside the caves for an unforgettable experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Zakynthos Marine Park area and Gerakas Beach – a protected loggerhead sea turtle nesting site. Enjoy a peaceful afternoon on this pristine, uncrowded beach. Optionally, join a guided turtle-watching experience with a local marine biologist.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a clifftop bar overlooking the Ionian Sea. Enjoy a farewell Zakynthos dinner at a traditional Greek taverna with live bouzouki music.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the Zakynthos hotel – fresh pastries, Greek omelette, cold cuts, and freshly squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at a premium taverna near Gerakas Beach – grilled fish, Greek salad, tzatziki, and local white wine
meals.dinner: Traditional Zakynthian dinner at a premium taverna – sofrito (Zakynthos-style veal), fresh pasta with seafood, and local Verdea wine

day_by_day.notes: The Blue Caves are best visited before 11:00 AM for the most vivid light effects. Gerakas Beach has restricted access during turtle nesting season (June–August) – follow all park guidelines. Confirm return transport to mainland or next destination.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Zakynthos to Heraklion, Crete (or take a connecting flight). Arrange a private luxury transfer to your premium accommodation in Crete – ideally a boutique villa or five-star resort on the southern or western coast near Elafonissi.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in and settle into your Cretan accommodation. Spend the afternoon by the pool or at the hotel beach, enjoying the warm Cretan sun. Visit a nearby winery for a private wine tasting of Cretan varieties such as Vidiano and Kotsifali.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nearest Cretan village or town on foot. Visit a local agora (market) and pick up Cretan olive oil, herbs, and cheeses as souvenirs. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at a traditional Cretan meze restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the Zakynthos hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium restaurant near the Heraklion airport or en route to the accommodation – Cretan dakos salad, lamb with stamnagathi greens, and local beer
meals.dinner: Dinner at a premium Cretan taverna – slow-roasted lamb, wild greens with olive oil, Cretan cheese platter, and Cretan raki to finish

day_by_day.notes: Book flights from Zakynthos to Heraklion well in advance as they can fill up quickly in June. Arrange private airport transfer in Crete. Consider renting a private car in Crete for flexibility.

day_by_day.morning: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip: Depart early by private car to Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete (approximately 75 km from Chania). Arrive before the crowds to experience the magical pink-tinged sand and shallow turquoise lagoon at its most serene. Wade across the shallow sandbar to the small island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying Elafonissi Beach – swim, snorkel, and relax on the unique rose-colored sands. The water is warm, crystal clear, and exceptionally calm, making it ideal for swimming. Explore the sand dunes and natural rock formations.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Chania or your resort. Stop at a clifftop taverna along the coastal road for a sundowner with views of the Libyan Sea. Return to the resort for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure – Greek yogurt, honey, nuts, fresh fruit, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by the resort or a beachside taverna near Elafonissi – fresh sandwiches, Cretan cheese pies (kalitsounia), fruit, and water
meals.dinner: Dinner at a premium restaurant in Chania's old town or near the resort – fresh Cretan seafood, grilled octopus, and local white wine. Recommended: Tamam Restaurant or Portes

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Elafonissi before 9:00 AM to avoid peak crowds. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a beach umbrella, and plenty of water. The beach has limited shade. The drive from Chania is scenic but involves winding mountain roads – allow 90 minutes each way.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the historic old town of Chania with a private guide. Walk through the Venetian harbor, visit the lighthouse, and explore the covered market (Agora) of Chania for premium local products. Tour the Firkas Fortress and the Byzantine and Post-Byzantine Collection museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Balos Lagoon (approximately 55 km from Chania) via private boat from Kissamos port or by 4x4 vehicle. Balos features a stunning shallow lagoon with white sand and turquoise water. Swim and explore the cape with views of three seas meeting.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Chania for a premium evening. Enjoy sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar overlooking the Venetian harbor. Book a table at one of Chania's finest restaurants for a Cretan fine dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast – eggs any style, Cretan honey pie, fresh pastries, and cold-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Lunch at a taverna near Balos or a packed gourmet lunch box from the resort – Cretan pies, olives, cheese, and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Fine dining in Chania's old town – contemporary Cretan cuisine with a tasting menu featuring local ingredients. Recommended: To Maridaki or Ela

day_by_day.notes: The road to Balos by car is unpaved and requires a 4x4 vehicle; alternatively, take the boat from Kissamos for a more comfortable journey. Book the boat in advance. Chania's old town is best explored on foot – wear comfortable shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Samaria Gorge hike (optional for active travelers): Join a premium guided hiking experience through the Samaria Gorge, one of Europe's longest gorges (16 km). The hike descends through dramatic mountain scenery and ends at the village of Agia Roumeli on the Libyan Sea. Alternatively, enjoy a relaxing spa morning at the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: For hikers: Take the ferry from Agia Roumeli to Sfakia, then transfer back to the resort. For non-hikers: Enjoy a private beach afternoon with premium cabana service, water sports, and a resort spa treatment (hot stone massage or thalassotherapy).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private Cretan food and wine pairing experience at a local organic farm or olive estate. Learn about Cretan culinary traditions, taste estate-produced olive oil, local wines, and handmade cheeses.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before the hike – energy-rich foods including eggs, whole grain bread, nuts, and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet hiking lunch provided by the resort or purchased at a taverna in Agia Roumeli at the end of the gorge
meals.dinner: Farm-to-table dinner at the Cretan olive estate during the private food and wine pairing experience – slow-cooked lamb, fresh vegetables, artisan cheeses, and estate wine

day_by_day.notes: The Samaria Gorge hike is strenuous and takes 5–7 hours. Wear proper hiking shoes and bring plenty of water. The gorge is open from May to October. Non-hikers should book spa treatments in advance. The farm dinner experience should be reserved through the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise sailing excursion from a Cretan marina. Sail along the rugged Cretan coastline, discovering hidden sea caves, secluded beaches, and crystal-clear snorkeling spots. Enjoy breakfast on deck with freshly brewed coffee and pastries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark and visit the ancient Minoan Palace of Knossos near Heraklion with a private archaeologist guide for an in-depth premium tour. Explore the 3,500-year-old ruins of Europe's oldest civilization and the fascinating Heraklion Archaeological Museum.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a final Cretan evening. Enjoy a premium sunset dinner at the resort's beach restaurant, toasting to the trip with a bottle of Cretan Assyrtiko or Vidiano. Arrange packing and confirm departure logistics with the concierge.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast served on deck during the morning sailing excursion – fresh pastries, smoked salmon, fruits, yogurt, and coffee
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at a restaurant near Knossos or in Heraklion – stuffed vine leaves, grilled meats, Cretan salad, and local wine
meals.dinner: Farewell Cretan dinner at the resort's beach restaurant – premium tasting menu with wine pairing, featuring the best of Cretan gastronomy

day_by_day.notes: Book the private sailing charter and Knossos private guide in advance. The Heraklion Archaeological Museum is one of the finest in Europe – allow at least 2 hours. Confirm next-day departure arrangements with the resort concierge tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Greece – enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the resort. Take one final swim in the Aegean or Cretan Sea, soak in the last views of the turquoise water, and complete any last-minute souvenir shopping (local olive oil, saffron, honey, and Cretan herbs make excellent gifts).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the resort. Private luxury transfer to Heraklion International Airport (or Athens, depending on return flight routing). Allow ample time for check-in and security. Enjoy a final Greek coffee and pastry at the airport lounge.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Greece. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of beaches, food, history, and Aegean beauty.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast – full spread including Greek specialties, fresh juices, pastries, and coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport premium lounge or a quick bite at a quality airport restaurant – Greek salad, pita with hummus, and fresh juice
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 12:00 PM – arrange a late checkout if possible for a relaxed morning. Confirm all transfer bookings the night before. Keep a small amount of euros for airport purchases. Ensure all purchased local goods are properly packed to comply with airline regulations.
